case_name: Abdul Latif v Abdul Hamid and another
respondent:
Abdul Hamid and another
Supreme Court of India

15 February 2002
C.A. Nos. 1343-1344 of 2002
The Judgment was delivered by : U. C. Banerjee, J.
1. Leave granted.
Upon hearing the submissions made on behalf of the parties and having regard to the notices issued, we do feel it inclined not to record our concurrence with the judgment of the High Court.
2. Before, however, dealing with the matter any further, we wish to place on record our displeasure in the matter by reason of the suppression of material facts in the petition before the Apex Court u/art. 136 of the Constitution. The petitions are totally silent as regards the filing of the second review petition before the High Court.

facts: The petitions are totally silent as regards the filing of the second review petition before the High Court.
In filing the petitions before this Court, it is the duty incumbent and obligation upon the advocate to place on record the entire set of facts faithfully and without any concoction therein.
There was suppression of material facts in the petition before the Apex Court u/art. 136 of the Constitution.
The statutory provisions have not been properly dealt with and thus cannot be sustained.
petitioner_arguments: We do feel it inclined not to record our concurrence with the judgment of the High Court.
court_reasoning: The justice delivery system of this country does not deprive anybody to receive the justice on the ground of technicalities alone and on account of fact that justice-oriented approach in this system is the hall-mark
We desist from dismissing these appeals on this ground alone.
As noticed above that there was suppression of facts and since we have, for the sake of the concept of justice, given a go-bye to such a technicality in our view
holding: The orders impugned before this Court stand set aside and quashed.

The appeals stand remanded to the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, (Lucknow Bench), for being dealt with in accordance with law upon framing of a substantial question of law in terms of S. 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

These appeals are allowed upon, however, payment of costs assessed at Rs. 2,500 to be paid by the appellant to the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee within a period of four weeks from the date hereof.
